Practice identifying a fire hazard, raising the alarm, avoiding the danger zone, evacuating safely, and extinguishing a small fire.
A fire has broken out near the machinery. Tap the fire to acknowledge the hazard.
Hazard identified. Stay calm and follow procedure.
You must identify the fire before proceeding.
Look for flames and smoke near the machinery ahead of you.
Activate the fire alarm to alert other workers in the area.
Alarm activated. Other workers have been alerted.
The alarm was not activated correctly.
The alarm panel is mounted on the wall, marked with a red light.
Stay clear of the marked hazard zone around the fire while you plan your next move.
Good — you kept a safe distance from the fire.
You entered the hazard zone. This is a critical safety violation.
Keep at least the marked distance away from the flames.
Follow the AR arrow to the nearest marked safe exit.
You reached the safe evacuation point.
You did not reach the exit in time.
Follow the direction the arrow is pointing.
Select the correct fire extinguisher for an electrical/chemical fire (CO2, Class B/C).
Correct choice — CO2 extinguishers are safe for electrical/chemical fires.
Wrong extinguisher type — water or foam can be dangerous on this kind of fire.
Water conducts electricity — avoid it near machinery fires.
Aim at the base of the fire and use the extinguisher.
Fire extinguished. Emergency procedure complete.
The fire was not extinguished correctly.
Sweep the extinguisher nozzle across the base of the flames, not the top.
Gas Leak / Confined Space Emergency
Practice identifying a gas leak, keeping a safe distance, selecting correct PPE, following the buddy system, reporting the emergency, and evacuating to the assembly point.
A gas leak has been detected near the confined space entrance. Tap the leak source to acknowledge the hazard.
Hazard identified. Do not approach the confined space.
You must identify the gas leak before proceeding.
Look for the visible gas/vapor cloud near the entrance.
Stay outside the marked hazard zone while you assess the situation.
Good — you maintained a safe distance from the leak.
You entered the gas hazard zone without protection. This is a critical safety violation.
Keep at least the marked distance away from the confined space entrance.
Select the correct PPE before any further action: full respirator and gas-detection kit.
Correct — full respirator and gas detector equipped.
Incomplete or missing PPE is not safe for a gas hazard area.
A dust mask or partial gear is not enough for a gas leak.
Confined space entry rules require a buddy. Choose how you will proceed.
Correct — never enter a confined space alone.
Entering alone violates confined-space entry procedure. This is a critical safety violation.
Confined space entry always requires at least one other trained worker on standby.
Report the leak to the control room before any further action is taken.
Control room notified. Isolation procedure has started.
The leak must be reported to the control room immediately.
Use the radio/emergency panel to contact the control room.
Follow the AR arrow to the designated safe assembly point.
You reached the safe assembly point. Emergency procedure complete.
You did not reach the assembly point in time.
Follow the direction the arrow is pointing, away from the hazard zone.
What should you do first when you discover a fire?
Try to extinguish it yourself
Identify the hazard and stay calm
Run immediately without alerting anyone
Ignore it if it looks small
Always identify and acknowledge the hazard first before taking further action.
Why should you activate the fire alarm even if you plan to fight the fire yourself?
It's not necessary if you're confident
To alert other workers so they can evacuate
Alarms are only for large fires
To satisfy a paperwork requirement
Raising the alarm ensures every worker in the area gets a chance to evacuate, regardless of how the fire is handled.
Which extinguisher type is safe to use on an electrical or chemical fire?
Water
Foam
CO2 (Class B/C)
Any extinguisher works the same
Water and foam can conduct electricity or react dangerously with chemical fires. CO2 extinguishers are the safe choice.
How close is it safe to stand near an active industrial fire without protective procedure?
As close as needed to see clearly
Only the marked safe distance away
Right next to it if you're quick
Distance doesn't matter indoors
Hazard zones are marked for a reason — staying outside the marked distance is a critical safety requirement, not a suggestion.
When using a fire extinguisher, where should you aim it?
At the top of the flames
At the smoke
At the base of the fire
Anywhere near the fire
Aiming at the base of the fire targets the fuel source directly, which is what actually puts the fire out.
What is the first step after detecting a gas leak near a confined space?
Enter to check the source
Acknowledge the hazard and stay outside the hazard zone
Wait for it to dissipate on its own
Continue working nearby
Identify the hazard first, then keep a safe distance — never approach a suspected gas leak directly.
What PPE is required before approaching a gas hazard area?
A dust mask is sufficient
No special PPE is needed for short exposure
Full respirator and gas-detection kit
Regular work gloves only
Partial protection like a dust mask does not protect against toxic or flammable gases — full respirator and detection equipment are required.
Why is the buddy system mandatory for confined space entry?
It's only a suggestion, not a rule
So someone can call for help if something goes wrong
To split the workload faster
It isn't actually required
Confined spaces can incapacitate a worker quickly (toxic atmosphere, oxygen deficiency) — a buddy on standby can raise the alarm and get help immediately.
What should happen before entering a confined space with a known gas leak?
Enter immediately to check for injuries
Report to the control room and wait for isolation procedures
Only tell your supervisor after the fact
Nothing — proceed as normal
The control room needs to be notified so isolation and monitoring procedures can begin before anyone enters.
What is the correct action if you accidentally enter the gas hazard zone without proper procedure?
Continue as if nothing happened
This is a critical safety violation — it should never happen and must be reported
It's fine as long as you don't smell anything
Only a problem if you feel dizzy
Entering a hazard zone without following procedure is treated as a critical safety failure — the exposure risk exists whether or not symptoms appear immediately.
